elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience at any time.
elements.evidence: Treating PB as Customer, the clause states that PB may terminate the Agreement “at any time,” with the prior funding-threshold and pre-approval-window conditions removed.

elements.element: Customer must give 30 days' notice of termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause requires sixty (60) days' prior notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires “prior written notice.”

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: No refund of prepaid fees is required. Instead, PB must pay SFJ 300% of Development Costs, and certain Approval Payments may remain payable.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not prohibit SFJ from terminating for convenience during a committed term, and the absence of such a right elsewhere in the Agreement is not demonstrated.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: PB may terminate the Agreement “at any time” by notice to SFJ.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period must be between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires sixty (60) days' prior written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Termination triggers a mandatory payment equal to 300% of all Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ, with possible continuing Approval Payments. No cap limiting the termination-related payment to three months' fees is included.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no operative restriction limiting SFJ's termination-for-convenience right to the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must give 90 days' notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: No 90-day notice requirement applicable to a termination for convenience by SFJ appears in the rendered clause.

result.reason: The redline successfully removes the funding-threshold and regulatory-window conditions and gives PB an unconditional right on 60 days' written notice. It nevertheless fails both positions because it provides no pro-rata refund, retains an uncapped termination-triggered payment of 300% of Development Costs, and adds no restrictions on SFJ's termination-for-convenience rights. The edit preserves the unrelated data-package and Approval Payment provisions without introducing an internal contradiction, but it is not a complete or minimal implementation of either playbook position.
